title: Large-Scale, Longitudinal Study of Large Language Models During the 2024 US Election Season

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to election-related queries by asking models to associate specific adjectives with presidential candidates, predicting exit poll outcomes to infer implicit beliefs about voter preferences, and measuring the cosine distance of response embeddings when prompted with explicit political affiliations (e.g., 'I am a Democrat' vs. 'I am a Republican').

Calculating the cosine distance of response embeddings to measure how election-related answers change when users self-identify with different racial and ethnic backgrounds (e.g., 'I am White', 'I am Black', 'I am Hispanic', 'I am Asian') in the prompt.

Calculating the cosine distance of response embeddings to measure model steerability and response variation when the prompt includes explicit gender identification (e.g., 'I identify as a man', 'I identify as a woman').
